reasonToGo: The one lobe anyone has WALKED that carries all three of the things Reedstrand lives on at once — c06/r05 carries the same three and nobody has set foot on it: open meadow to sow, six mires to cut, and standing wet wood. The swamp forest and the carr here are the only carr drawn off Wealdmarch — four of the world's five stand in the basin and the fifth is this one — so the timber worked here is the only carr-wood on the delta that has been reached.

hazards.name: The holed shelf
hazards.description: The marine terrace along the seaward edge is holed through to the water, and on a swell the hole blows. The two sets of workings named for it on the charts are named for the noise, which carries inland further than the ground it comes from can be seen.

hazards.name: The floating mat
hazards.description: One of the mires is not ground at all but a mat of root and moss grown across open water, and it looks from a distance exactly like the quaking bog beside it, which will at least hold for a step. There is no mark on either and no way to tell them apart from the bank.

resources.name: Lobe grain
resources.description: Sown broadcast on the meadow between the mires, which is five-sixths of this ground — though the delta's five reported lobes each carry three times the meadow this one does, and nobody has walked any of them. It is reaped early and always wet: there is nowhere on the lobe high enough to stook a sheaf, so the crop is carried green to the drying stacks on the terrace.

resources.name: Hag peat
resources.description: Cut out of the peat hag, the raised bog and the quaking bog, dried on the terrace beside the grain and burned in the same hearths. Six separate mires stand on this one region and no two of them cut the same: the crews name the bank a turf came out of when they sell it.

resources.name: Carr poles
resources.description: Alder and sallow off the swamp forest and the carr, cut standing in water and floated out rather than carried. It is the only wood anyone has walked to on Reedstrand that is not mangrove — one further stand is drawn on the delta and it is reported ground — and it is what every hurdle, creel and roof frame here is made of.

landmarks.name: Osierholm Quag
landmarks.description: The floating mire at the centre of the lobe, grown right across open water and firm enough at its edges to cut and nowhere near firm enough to cross. The cutting banks work in from the rim and stop where the mat begins, and the line they stop at moves every year.

landmarks.name: Head between Bitternstrand
landmarks.description: The blunt seaward end of the lobe between the barrier island and the bar, with the tidal flat inside it and the arch standing at its point. It is the last dry ground going out and the first going in, and every load off this region crosses it.
